subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should OpenClaw fix this as RPC-first/no-maintenance CLI access, a stricter single-writer shared-state DB lease, or a staged combination of both?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the durable fix changes ownership across gateway RPC, CLI recovery, doctor migrations, plugin-state probes, and operator repair behavior.

options.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should avoid journal, checkpoint, and migration side effects.

options.title: Single-writer gateway lease
options.body: The gateway should own shared-state write and maintenance access, with non-gateway processes failing closed or routing through explicit gateway/maintenance APIs.

options.title: Forensic harness first
options.body: Pause implementation until the reporter's preserved DB bundle and a native runtime harness confirm the exact helper/runtime interaction.

recommendation.title: RPC-first plus no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Status, health, and stability should ask the running gateway first, and fallback file opens while the gateway is active should avoid journal, checkpoint, and migration side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across the DB-first runtime-state architecture introduced in PR https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78595 and current gateway/CLI ownership boundaries.
